input.question: When did straight white teeth become a status symbol?
input.ground_truth: I'm guessing this is a thing in the States? As with so many things, it probably started to become a status symbol as soon as famous people started doing it. This being said, the super white teeth American TV stars and politicians tend to have is not really a thing here in Europe (is this changing?). So it's not a status symbol everywhere. Even teeth you take very good care of should have a slightly yellow tint to them. It's the natural color of the teeth. By making them completely white you're making them look like something that isn't the color of teeth.

Okay, let's imagine you have a toy box full of different toys. Some toys are shiny and new, and some are a little old and chipped. Now, a long time ago, having straight and white teeth wasn't something people thought was extra special or fancy. But as time went by, some people started thinking that straight and white teeth looked really nice and healthy, kind of like the shiny new toys.

In the old days, people didn't always have ways to make their teeth straight or white, so most teeth looked different. But when we got better at cleaning teeth and fixing them (like with braces), some people started showing off their straight and white teeth because it showed they could take care of themselves and maybe had more money to spend on nice things.

So, in the last 100 years or so, especially in some countries, straight and white teeth became like a "status symbol." That means it's seen as a sign that someone is healthy, rich, and takes good care of themselves, just like having the shiniest toy in the toy box.
